results.title: First unit literal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns the literal $\ell$ of the first clause of $\varphi$ that consists of the single literal $\ell$, and returns nothing when no clause of $\varphi$ has exactly one literal.

results.title: First variable of a CNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns the variable of the first literal of the first nonempty clause of $\varphi$, that is, the first variable occurring in $\varphi$ in source order, and returns nothing when every clause of $\varphi$ is empty (in particular when $\varphi$ has no clauses).

results.title: Rouché–Capelli theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ be a set and $n$ a finite set, let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over $K$, and let $b \in K^m$. Then the linear system $Ax = b$ has a solution $x \in K^n$ if and only if the rank of $A$ equals the rank of the augmented matrix $(A \mid b)$, whose columns are the columns of $A$ followed by the single column $b$.

results.title: Schur decomposition of a complex square matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a square complex matrix whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite linearly ordered type $n$. results.title: Primitive divisor of an integer sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let $m$ and $u$ be natural numbers. Then $u$ is a primitive divisor of $a_m$ when $m \ge 1$, $u \ge 2$, $u$ divides $a_m$, and $u$ divides no $a_s$ with $1 \le s < m$.

results.title: Primitive prime divisor of an integer sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let $m$ and $u$ be natural numbers. Then $u$ is a primitive prime divisor of $a_m$ when $u$ is prime and $u$ is a primitive divisor of $a_m$.

results.title: A primitive divisor appears at the least positive index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let the natural number $u$ be a primitive divisor of $a_m$. If $n \ge 1$ and $u$ divides $a_n$, then $m \le n$.

results.title: A primitive divisor occurs at only one index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers. If a natural number $u$ is a primitive divisor of both $a_m$ and $a_n$, then $m = n$.

results.title: A primitive prime divisor occurs at only one index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers. If a natural number $u$ is a primitive prime divisor of both $a_m$ and $a_n$, then $m = n$.

results.title: Primitive divisor relative to a discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ be a sequence of integers and let $D$ be an integer (for a Lucas pair $(\alpha, \beta)$, the discriminant $D = (\alpha - \beta)^2$). A natural number $p$ is a primitive divisor of $u_n$ when $n \ge 1$, $p$ is prime, $p$ divides $u_n$, and $p$ does not divide $D \, u_1 u_2 \cdots u_{n-1}$ (for $n = 1$ the product is empty, and the condition is that $p$ does not divide $D$).

results.title: Euler's theorem on odd perfect numbers

results.title: Bound on $H(n)$ for primitive non-deficient numbers by the least prime factor

results.title: Fifth-power bound on the Euler prime of an odd perfect number

results.title: Refined fifth-power bound on the Euler prime of an odd perfect number

results.title: Caristi fixed-point theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(X, d)$ be a nonempty complete metric space and let $\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$ be lower semicontinuous and bounded below. If a map $T : X \to X$ satisfies $d(x, T x) \le \varphi(x) - \varphi(T x)$ for every $x \in X$, then $T$ has a fixed point: there is $x \in X$ with $T x = x$.

results.title: Thick set in a commutative semigroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ is thick when for every finite set $E \subseteq S$ there is an $x \in S$ with $E + x \subseteq A$, that is, $e + x \in A$ for every $e \in E$.

results.title: Piecewise syndetic set in a commutative semigroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ is piecewise syndetic when there is a finite set $F \subseteq S$ such that the union $\bigcup_{t \in F} (-t + A)$ is thick, where $-t + A = \{s \in S : t + s \in A\}$.

results.title: J-sets in commutative semigroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a commutative semigroup and let $\mathbb{N} = \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$. A set $A \subseteq S$ is a $J$-set when for every finite set $F$ of sequences $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to S$ there are $a \in S$ and a nonempty finite set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $a + \sum_{n \in H} f(n) \in A$ for every $f \in F$.

results.title: CR-set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative semigroup $(S, +)$ is a CR-set (combinatorially rich) when for every natural number $n$, including $n = 0$, there is a natural number $r$ such that for every $r \times n$ matrix $(m_{ij})$ with entries in $S$ there are a nonempty set $\alpha \subseteq \{1, \ldots, r\}$ and an element $s \in S$ such that $s + \sum_{i \in \alpha} m_{ij} \in A$ for every column $j \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$.

results.title: Essential CR-set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $(S, +)$ be a commutative semigroup, and add ultrafilters on $S$ by the rule that $E \in p + q$ if and only if $\{x \in S : \{y \in S : x + y \in E\} \in q\} \in p$. A subset $A$ of $S$ is an essential CR-set when there is an ultrafilter $p$ on $S$ with $p + p = p$, all of whose members are CR-sets, such that $A \in p$.

results.title: Families with the Ramsey property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $S$ be a set. A collection $F$ of subsets of $S$ is a family with the Ramsey property when $F$ is nonempty, $\emptyset \notin F$, $F$ is closed under supersets (if $A \in F$ and $A \subseteq B$, then $B \in F$), and whenever $A \cup B \in F$, then $A \in F$ or $B \in F$.

results.title: The set β(F) of ultrafilters inside a family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of a set $S$, $\beta(\mathcal F)$ is the set of ultrafilters $p$ on $S$ all of whose members lie in $\mathcal F$, that is, $A \in \mathcal F$ for every $A \in p$.

results.title: Membership in β(F)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a collection of subsets of a set $S$ and let $p$ be an ultrafilter on $S$. Then $p \in \beta(F)$ if and only if every member of $p$ belongs to $F$.

results.title: β of the nonempty sets is all of βS
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $S$, every ultrafilter on $S$ lies in $\beta(\mathcal F)$, where $\mathcal F$ is the family of all nonempty subsets of $S$; that is, $\beta(\mathcal F) = \beta S$, the set of all ultrafilters on $S$.

results.title: Ultrafilters inside a Ramsey family form a closed set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a family of subsets of a set $S$ with the Ramsey property. Then the set $\beta(F)$ of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $F$ is closed in the space $\beta S$ of all ultrafilters on $S$.

results.title: Theorem 3, part 2: a Ramsey family is the union of its ultrafilters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a family of subsets of a set $S$ with the Ramsey property, and let $\beta(F)$ be the set of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $F$. Then a set $A \subseteq S$ lies in $F$ if and only if $A \in p$ for some $p \in \beta(F)$; that is, $F = \bigcup \beta(F)$.

results.title: Nonempty closed sets of ultrafilters come from Ramsey families
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a set, let $\beta S$ be the space of ultrafilters on $S$, and let $K$ be a nonempty closed subset of $\beta S$. Let $\mathcal F_K$ be the collection of the sets $E \subseteq S$ with $E \in p$ for some $p \in K$. Then $\mathcal F_K$ is a family with the Ramsey property, and $\beta(\mathcal F_K) = K$, where $\beta(\mathcal F_K)$ is the set of ultrafilters on $S$ all of whose members lie in $\mathcal F_K$.

results.title: β(F) contains an idempotent when it is a subsemigroup

results.title: Subsemigroup criterion for β(F)
results.caption: Theorem

results.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns nothing if and only if $k$ is at least the length of $L$.

results.title: Median-of-medians selection agrees with sorting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ over a linearly ordered type and every natural number $k$, median-of-medians selection of rank $k$ in $L$ returns the entry at zero-based position $k$ of the insertion sort of $L$ by $\le$ when $k$ is less than the length of $L$, and returns nothing otherwise.

results.title: Set rank of a median-of-medians result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list without repeated entries over a linear order and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. If median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$, then the set $\{y \in L : y \le x\}$ has exactly $k + 1$ elements.

results.title: One-based rank of a median-of-medians result
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list without repeated entries over a linear order and let $i \ge 1$. If median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $i - 1$ returns an element $x$, then the set $\{y \in L : y \le x\}$ has exactly $i$ elements.

results.title: Median of medians selects every one-based rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a list without repeated entries over a linear order, of length $n$, and let $1 \le i \le n$. Then median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $i - 1$ returns an element $x$ of $L$, and the set $\{y \in L : y \le x\}$ has exactly $i$ elements.

results.title: Median of medians finds the lower median
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a nonempty list of length $n$ over a linear order, and let $k = \lfloor (n - 1)/2 \rfloor$. Then median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$ of $L$ such that at most $k$ entries of $L$ are less than $x$ and more than $k$ entries of $L$ are at most $x$, where entries are counted with repetition.

results.title: Median of medians finds the upper median
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a nonempty list of length $n$ over a linear order, and let $k = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. Then median-of-medians selection on $L$ at zero-based rank $k$ returns an element $x$ of $L$ such that at most $k$ entries of $L$ are less than $x$ and more than $k$ entries of $L$ are at most $x$, where entries are counted with repetition.

results.title: Size budget for the two median-of-medians recursive calls
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $m$ and $p$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 140$, $m \le \lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor$ and $p \le \lfloor 7n/10 \rfloor + 6$. Then $20m + 20p + n \le 20n$.

results.title: Cost budget for one median-of-medians step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $m$, $p$, $a$, $c_1$ and $c_2$ be natural numbers with $n \ge 140$, $m \le \lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor$, $p \le \lfloor 7n/10 \rfloor + 6$, $c_1 \le 20am$ and $c_2 \le 20ap$. Then $c_1 + c_2 + an \le 20an$.

results.title: Median of medians makes linearly many comparisons
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $L$ of length $n$ over a linear order and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, median-of-medians selection on $L$ at rank $k$ charges at most $80n$ comparisons, where $n$ counts repeated entries.

results.title: Linear solution of the median-of-medians recurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $a \in \mathbb{N}$. Suppose that $T(n) \le 20an$ for every $n \le 140$, and that for every $n > 140$ there are $m, p \in \mathbb{N}$ with $m \le \lfloor (n + 4)/5 \rfloor$, $p \le \lfloor 7n/10 \rfloor + 6$ and $T(n) \le T(m) + T(p) + an$. Then $T(n) \le 20an$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Finite joint law
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A finite joint law consists of positive integers $n_X$ and $n_Y$ and a probability distribution on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\} \times \{0, \dots, n_Y - 1\}$.

results.title: Input law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The input law of a finite joint law $p$ on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\} \times \{0, \dots, n_Y - 1\}$ is its first marginal: the law on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\}$ that is the image of $p$ under $(x, y) \mapsto x$.

results.title: Output law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The output law of a finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ is the law of $Y$: the marginal of $p$ on the output alphabet, obtained by pushing $p$ forward along the projection onto the second coordinate.

results.title: Mutual information
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mutual information of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ is $I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X, Y)$, where $H(X)$ and $H(Y)$ are the Shannon entropies in bits of the input and output laws of $p$, and $H(X, Y)$ is the Shannon entropy in bits of $p$.

results.title: Finite extension of a joint law
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A finite extension of a finite joint law $p$ on $\{0, \dots, n_X - 1\} \times \{0, \dots, n_Y - 1\}$ consists of a positive integer $n_S$ and a probability law on triples $(x, y, s)$ with $s \in \{0, \dots, n_S - 1\}$ whose marginal on the pairs $(x, y)$ is exactly $p$.

results.title: Trivial extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The trivial extension of a finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ has the one-letter auxiliary alphabet $\{0\}$ and, as its law, the law of $((X, Y), 0)$ for $(X, Y)$ distributed according to $p$; its $(X, Y)$ marginal is $p$.

results.title: Auxiliary marginal of an extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite extension $q$ of a finite joint law $p$, viewed as the law of a triple $(X, Y, S)$ with $S$ taking values in $\{0, \dots, n_S - 1\}$, the auxiliary law is the marginal law of $S$ under $q$.

results.title: Input-auxiliary law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$, that is, a law of $((X, Y), S)$ with an auxiliary variable $S$. Its input-auxiliary law is the joint law of $(X, S)$: the image of the law of $q$ under $((x, y), s) \mapsto (x, s)$.

results.title: Output-auxiliary law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$, that is, a law of $((X, Y), S)$ with an auxiliary variable $S$. Its output-auxiliary law is the joint law of $(Y, S)$: the image of the law of $q$ under $((x, y), s) \mapsto (y, s)$.

results.title: Mutual information between the input and the auxiliary
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite extension $q$ of a finite joint law $p$, viewed as the law of a triple $(X, Y, S)$ whose $(X, Y)$ marginal is $p$, this is $I(X; S) = H(X) + H(S) - H(X, S)$, where $H(X)$ is the Shannon entropy in bits of the $X$ marginal of $p$, and $H(S)$ and $H(X, S)$ are the Shannon entropies in bits of the $S$ and $(X, S)$ marginals of $q$.

results.title: Conditional entropy of the output given the auxiliary
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite extension $q$ of a finite joint law $p$, viewed as the law of a triple $(X, Y, S)$ whose $(X, Y)$ marginal is $p$, this is $H(Y \mid S) = H(Y, S) - H(S)$, where $H(Y, S)$ and $H(S)$ are the Shannon entropies in bits of the $(Y, S)$ and $S$ marginals of $q$.

results.title: Conditional entropy of the output given the input and the auxiliary
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite extension of a finite joint law, with input $X$, output $Y$ and auxiliary $S$, the conditional entropy of $Y$ given $(X, S)$ is $H(Y \mid X, S) = H(X, Y, S) - H(X, S)$, where $H$ denotes Shannon entropy in bits, $H(X, Y, S)$ is the entropy of the law of the extension and $H(X, S)$ is the entropy of its $(X, S)$ marginal.

results.title: Zero output entropy given input and auxiliary for a one-letter output
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a finite joint law of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ whose output alphabet has exactly one letter. Then for every finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary $S$, the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid X, S)$ of the output given the input and the auxiliary is $0$.

results.title: Auxiliary law of the trivial extension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite joint law $p$, the auxiliary law of the trivial extension of $p$ is the point mass at $0$, the only letter of its one-letter auxiliary alphabet $\{0\}$.

results.title: The trivial extension has zero auxiliary information
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite joint law $p$, the mutual information $I(X; S)$ between the input $X$ and the auxiliary $S$ in the trivial extension of $p$, whose auxiliary alphabet has a single letter, is $0$.

results.title: Conditional entropy in the trivial extension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite joint law $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$, the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ of the output given the auxiliary $S$ in the trivial extension of $p$ equals the Shannon entropy $H(Y)$ of the output law of $p$.

results.title: Input marginal of the input-auxiliary law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $X$ under the joint law of $(X, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $X$ under $p$.

results.title: Output marginal of the output-auxiliary law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $Y$ under the joint law of $(Y, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $Y$ under $p$.

results.title: Auxiliary marginal of the input-auxiliary law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $S$ under the joint law of $(X, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $S$ in $q$.

results.title: Auxiliary marginal of the output-auxiliary law
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $q$ be a finite extension of a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$ by an auxiliary variable $S$. Then the marginal of $S$ under the joint law of $(Y, S)$ in $q$ equals the law of $S$ in $q$.

results.title: Conditional entropy vanishes for a one-letter output
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the output alphabet of a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$ has exactly one element, then for every finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$, the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ is $0$.

results.title: Conditional-prefix optimum of a joint law
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$, this is the infimum in the extended reals of the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ in bits over all finite extensions of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$ such that $I(X; S) = 0$ and $H(Y \mid X, S) = 0$. The infimum of the empty set is $+\infty$.

results.title: Worst-case conditional-prefix optimum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $t$, the worst-case optimum at $t$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ over all finite joint laws $p$ of an input $X$ and an output $Y$ whose mutual information $I(X; Y)$, in bits, equals $t$; it is $-\infty$ when no such law exists.

results.title: Channel simulation constant

results.title: Each admissible extension bounds the conditional-prefix optimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a finite joint law of $(X, Y)$ and let $q$ be a finite extension of $p$ by an auxiliary variable $S$ with $I(X; S) = 0$ and $H(Y \mid X, S) = 0$. Then the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ is at most the conditional entropy $H(Y \mid S)$ of $q$.

results.title: The conditional-prefix optimum vanishes for a one-letter output
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the output alphabet of a finite joint law $p$ has exactly one element, then the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ equals $0$.

results.title: The worst-case optimum dominates each conditional-prefix optimum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite joint law $p$ of $(X, Y)$, the conditional-prefix optimum of $p$ is at most the worst-case optimum at $t = I(X; Y)$, the mutual information of $p$ in bits.
